newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends mixed on Tokyo holiday.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends mixed on Tokyo holiday.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended mixed in quiet trading as buyers stayed away following the closure of the Tokyo market.

"It was basically drifting without buying interest," said a dealer, describing the quiet morning and evening session on the domestic market after Tokyo futures were untraded due to a national holiday.
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board qouted December RSS1 buyer at 319.50 cents ($1.26) a kg, up two cents from Friday's close. December SMR 20 was a cent lower at 310.
A dealer predicted on Friday, after some mild shortcovering, that prices may jump five to 10 percent across the board this week if the weather stayed wet and demand persisted.
Traders retained Friday's offer prices, quoting the SMR CV at 363, SMR L at 343, SMR 5 at 320, SMR10 at 308, SMR 20 at 307 and drum latex at 234.
The INRO five-day moving average rose to 243.09 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Nov 1 from 242.04 on Oct 31. The daily indicator price was at 244.76 against 244.36.
